ruling: DUPLICATION IS A DEFECT — but the remedy is a SHARED PARSER, not a conformance suite. Skillranker's apparatus (versioned adapters, contract matrix, capability fixtures) serves EXTERNAL plural implementations across versions; ours are three first-party readers (324 lines total) in one repo under one lane. Testing three implementations for agreement preserves the thing that diverges; having one implementation removes it. Do not copy the matrix; take the lesson (contract matters) at our scale (one module).

shared_parser_contract.golden_transcripts: one synthetic session exercising markers, no-markers, empty content, missing usage, multi-assistant turns — all consumers must agree on turns/sessions/counts exactly
shared_parser_contract.module: single session-reader (JSONL rows → messages → turns + usage extraction, ~80 lines); per-tool analyses stay separate (counterfactual pricing, lever shares, scenario bounds)
shared_parser_contract.open_design_decision_for_implementer: the turn definition itself (marker-pair rule with no-marker fallback, matching backtest's planted-arm rule, is the recommended default — not mandated here)
shared_parser_contract.tests: golden agreement assertions ride with the module, not in three places

skillranker_read: adapter_contract.rs (per-adapter contract version + conformance cells with evidence), contract_matrix.toml (boundaries → test IDs → owners), capabilities.v1.json fixture. Built for external adapter authors across versions — correctly heavy for that job, disproportionate for ours.

why_now.defect_class: OBSERVED, not speculative — turn-count divergence already bit twice (A02 unrelocatable turn-boundary miss; three artifacts asserting three counts for one fixture, PLAN §5.1 open defect). This clears the creation-gate bar.
why_now.scale: 3 readers, 324 lines, one repo, one owner-lane. A shared parser is an hour's refactor; the next divergence debug costs more than that.
